clue.text: Trees and fruit held by the presbyter

definitions.note: the office a presbyter holds, not the person

parts.note: elders are small trees of the honeysuckle family
a hip is the fruit of the wild rose

explanation.surface: A church elder keeps an orchard of trees and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the office a presbyter holds: elders in Presbyterian churches hold this position.
explanation.definitionFit: A presbyter is a church elder, and the rank or office he holds is named after that title.

clue.text: Top Conservative invested in old railway

indicators.note: the Conservative letter is placed inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: ex means former or old
an el is an elevated railway

explanation.surface: A leading Tory put money into a defunct railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a verb meaning to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or outdo others is to be outstanding.

clue.text: Rare din made in the kitchen

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new word

explanation.surface: An unusual racket is created among the pots and pans.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: something found in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack or colander for letting washed dishes or food drip dry is a kitchen item.

clue.text: Move back tree, perhaps, without upsetting stage scenery

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the tree letters surround the rest
the tree letters are taken in a possible new order
in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: décor is stage scenery

explanation.surface: A tree is moved backwards without knocking over the stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns TREE into RETE; 'upsetting' makes DECOR into ROCED, which sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede again or cede back is to go or give back, a retreat.

clue.text: Description of Greek culture from a woman in his movement

indicators.note: the woman goes inside the word his

parts.note: Ellen is a woman's name
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A woman joins a man's campaign spreading Greek civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers Greek culture after Alexander the Great, spread through the Mediterranean world.

clue.text: Equality is absent from the capital

indicators.note: the word is is taken away from the capital

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: Equal rights are missing in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is absent from' tells us IS is removed from PARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a level, as in at par, is a state of equal value.

clue.text: Sort of stitch many accomplished

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a crossword stand-in for many
able means skilled or accomplished

explanation.surface: A knitter is told this stitch takes great skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitting pattern of twisted, rope-like ridges is named after a thick wire rope.

clue.text: Fellow-printers' dance

parts.note: co- as in co-worker means fellow
the NGA was the National Graphical Association, the printers' trade union

explanation.surface: Members of the printers' union dance together.
explanation.walkthrough: The NGA was a British printing union until 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American line routine in which people follow each other with a kick on the beat.

clue.text: Treacherous woman accepts directions to act like 12

indicators.note: the woman takes the directions inside her

parts.note: bitch is a slang term for a malicious woman
E and W are the compass points east and west

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman takes instructions on how to cast spells.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is ENCHANTER, so acting like one means casting a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer casts spells, and to put someone under a spell is to enchant them.

clue.text: Putting up with imprisonment in support of Egyptian extremists

indicators.note: in a down clue the support piece sits under what it holds up
the outermost letters of the word are its extremes

parts.note: durance is an old word for imprisonment

explanation.surface: Someone bears a long jail term propping up Egyptian radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egyptian extremists' gives E and N; 'in support of' puts DURANCE below them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing hardship patiently is the power of lasting through, a noun for tolerance.

clue.text: A way to divide the fuel of the sea-shore

indicators.note: the fuel word is split apart so the other pieces can sit between its halves

parts.note: coal is the classic fuel
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone works out how to split the fuel supply of a seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to the coast lies along the shore of the sea.

clue.text: Chateaubriand married and began again

parts.note: the French writer was François-René de Chateaubriand, so his given name supplies the letters
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: The French author got married and started his life over.
explanation.walkthrough: Chateaubriand looks like the steak; here it is the writer, whose first name is René.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to start it afresh, so the past form means restarted.

clue.text: Fashionable attempt to follow student's jargon

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student
in means fashionable
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A trendy try at copying student slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts IN and GO after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang or specialist talk is informally called by this word for a foreign or peculiar tongue.

clue.text: Charmer's fashions entrance husband

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A charming man's style captivates a married man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashions' looks like a noun and 'entrance' like a verb; ENTRANCE plus H is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer who casts spells is one who charms, in the magical sense.

clue.text: She has the room prepared, we hear

indicators.note: says the phrase is a sound-alike of the answer

parts.note: a chamber is a room, and made means prepared, as a bed is made

explanation.surface: A hotel worker gets the room ready, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel maid who cleans bedrooms is a woman, so a pronoun for a female fits.

clue.text: Sailor employed in preservation of timber

definitions.meaning: the black pitch used to coat and protect wood

explanation.definitionFit: The slang word for a seaman is also the black pitchy substance painted on wood to protect it.

clue.text: One taking steps to re-create the Water Music?

definitions.text: One taking steps to re-create the Water Music?

parts.words: One taking steps to re-create the Water Music?
parts.note: a performer whose steps make a rhythm, with the water from a faucet rather than Handel's suite

explanation.definitionFit: A performer in metal-toed shoes makes music with the feet, and a faucet is a source of water.

clue.text: A blaze in the resort Raleigh described thus

indicators.note: read as re-sort, the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A fire breaks out in a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a seaside town; read as re-sort it rearranges A BLAZE IN THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh lived in the reign of the first Queen Elizabeth, so he is of that era.

clue.text: Kind of college reader in English at Leeds, originally

indicators.note: the reader goes in among the other letters
the original, first letters of the words are taken

parts.note: a lector is a reader, in church or a university

explanation.surface: A lecturer in English at Leeds university.
explanation.walkthrough: The US electoral college chooses the president.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of electors that formally chooses the US president is this kind of college.

clue.text: On hand, competent and fit to be seen

parts.note: present means on hand, there
able means competent

explanation.surface: A capable, available person is decent enough to be seen in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tidy enough to appear in company is acceptable in appearance.

clue.text: Big Mouth is in France, providing university with a transport system

parts.note: est is French for is
RY is short for railway

explanation.surface: A gossip in France arranges college travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A river's wide tidal outlet to the sea is a large mouth.

clue.text: The novel Haggard started in Kent?.

indicators.note: the starting letter goes inside the Kent letters

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England, SE

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Rider Haggard begins writing his novel in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: H.Rider Haggard wrote the novel 'She'; H goes inside SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rider Haggard's famous adventure book about Ayesha bears this pronoun as its title.

clue.text: In South Africa, desire to catch fine sea creature

indicators.note: the desire word takes the fine letter inside it

parts.note: a wish is a desire
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: In South Africa an angler longs to land a good fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray with a long toothed snout like a saw is a marine fish.

clue.text: "Another lean unwash'd ——" (K John)

parts.note: a line from Shakespeare's King John, Act 4, with the last word left blank to fill in

explanation.walkthrough: Hubert describes a craftsman spreading rumours: 'Another lean unwash'd artificer cuts off his tale'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line names a skilled workman or craftsman.

clue.text: Noisy bird, though physically weak

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a rail is a marsh bird

explanation.surface: A loud bird that is nonetheless feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone delicate or infirm lacks bodily strength.

clue.text: Absorbent cloth made of fibres by the Spanish

parts.note: tow is coarse flax or hemp fibre
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish-made fabric that soaks up water.
explanation.definitionFit: A drying cloth for the body or dishes is made to soak up water.

clue.text: Put name in the right shirts etc

indicators.note: the name letter is put inside the right

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Someone labels the correct shirts with a name tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link; a LIEN is a legal right.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirts, sheets and underwear are collectively called after the flax cloth they were once made of.

clue.text: Tea unusually dear? What an absurd pretence!

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: the letters of the word are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Someone protests at the outrageous price of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A transparent sham or farce is a mere play-acting.

clue.text: Urge, for instance, to conceal a key

indicators.note: the key letter is hidden inside the for-instance letters

parts.note: G is a musical key

explanation.surface: An example of hiding a key.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on is to goad, as in to egg on.

clue.text: Publicly accuse soldier retreating in Scottish isle

indicators.note: the turned soldier letters go inside the isle

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: a retreating soldier goes backwards, so his letters are read in reverse

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier falling back on a Scottish island is publicly denounced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns GI into IG, which goes inside ARRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone formally in court is to call them to answer an indictment.

clue.text: Two men of more than normal size

parts.note: Roy is a man's name
Al is a second man's name

explanation.surface: A pair of men who are unusually large.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal is a paper size bigger than standard, and the word also means splendidly large.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for kingly is also used for things larger or grander than usual, as in a large paper size.

clue.text: One-time Lord Treasurer's dismissal of a swimmer?

parts.note: go! is a curt dismissal
a dolphin is a swimming sea mammal

explanation.surface: A former finance minister sends a swimmer packing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sidney Godolphin was Lord High Treasurer under Queen Anne; the clue reads his name as 'Go, dolphin!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney, first Earl of that name, held the office of Lord High Treasurer around 1700.
